newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Large arms cache found in Nicaragua.
newsitem.headline: Large arms cache found in Nicaragua.

text.p: A large arms cache containing weapons and explosives was found on the farm of a former Sandinista army officer outside Nicaragua's capital, police said on Monday.

The arms cache, one of the largest found in Nicaragua since the end of its civil war in 1990, was discovered on Sunday on the property of retired Maj. Pilar Antonio Aguilar Loaisiga, 11 miles (17 kms) southwest of Managua, police commissioner Eduardo Cuadra Ferrey told a news conference.
Ferrey said the origin and intended purpose of the weapons were not known, and police investigations would continue.

The cache contained 134 rifles, nine submachine guns, 19 anti-personnel mines, 203 grenades, 683 seven-ounce (200-gram) sticks of dynamite, 622 14-ounce (400-gram) sticks of dynamite, 40 pounds (18 kgs) of dynamite in bags, 137 rolls of plastic explosives, 41 rocket launchers and more than 3,700 pounds (1,700 kgs) of ammunition, he said.
"The arms were in good condition; they were properly stored and could have been used at any moment," he said.
He said of the more than 15 arms caches found in Nicaragua since 1990, this one contained the most explosives, but others contained more weapons.
Police have detained the farm's caretaker, who apparently was unaware of the arms cache, but Aguilar remained at large, Ferrey said.
The weapons, found in a storeroom on the property, had likely been there more than two years, he said.
Many of the arms caches found in Nicaragua in the past were weapons stored in Nicaragua by El Salvador's left-wing guerrillas after the end of its civil war in 1992.
El Salvador had often accused Nicaragua's left-wing Sandinista Front, which governed Nicaragua from 1979 to 1990, of supporting and providing asylumn for the guerrillas.
